title: Human-guided active learning improves nickel-cobalt methanation tests
summary: A human-in-the-loop model selected nickel-cobalt catalysts and reaction settings for a 48-test laboratory campaign. Further selected experiments improved methane space-time yield by nearly 50% over the previous maximum in that dataset. Extrapolation remained harder than interpolation. This is a bounded catalyst-and-condition result, not evidence of industrial deployment or lifecycle climate benefit.
ai_technology: Gaussian-process active learning with batch acquisition

evidence.tested: Selected catalysts and conditions were experimentally tested; model-suggested activity trends received follow-up.
evidence.unknown: Generality, industrial durability and lifecycle carbon benefit were not established.
evidence.ai_role: Gaussian-process active learning with batch acquisition supported the stated study; experimental and interpretive work remained with researchers.

source_review.scope: Indexed primary publisher abstract, model Methods, selected Results, affiliations and first-online date; supplementary material not reviewed.
